analysis:
All supplied units are test-only files under provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Autopilot/: three new suites (SelectedModelRecoveryPolicyTests, SelectedModelRecoveryTests, SelectedModelRecoveryVictimTests) and a modified UnreclaimableLoadMemoryFixture. The fixture changes add a thread-safe ScriptedCounter and a superLoads counter on the stubbed Super loader. residentBytes now has a Super case, and the stub loader still always throws. No production code, endpoints, crypto, attestation, authorization or coordinator-wire behavior is changed. The tests use stub engines, a temporary directory and a scripted memory model. They carry no secrets and make no network calls.

The tests document intended production behavior in a recovery feature whose source is not in this batch. They cover eviction only of idle, non-selected, non-pinned, non-leased models past dwell and idle thresholds. They also cover never evicting models in the running selection, and no retry after a non-memory refusal. Those are availability and resource-policy properties relevant to TB-007 and T-029. They do not touch T-041 cache storage or the TB-002/TB-011 contracts.

Remaining integration question: the production recovery implementation (checkSelectedModelRecoveryIfDue, enqueueSelectedModelRecovery, and the eviction and victim rules) was not supplied. Whether it enforces these test expectations, and whether it interacts safely with in-flight requests and residual GPU data (T-028), cannot be assessed here. No regression is identifiable from the test files alone.
